# Live /blogs/ URLs for pages created AFTER the blog-priv#62 URL migration.
#
# Why this file exists. scripts/test_permalink_contract.py asserts AC 5.2 in two
# directions: every retired URL still resolves onto a live one (the half that
# matters, and that stays untouched), AND every live /blogs/ URL is the image of
# some retired URL. The second direction is only meaningful as a staleness check
# on the migration snapshot itself. Read literally it also says "no page may ever
# be added again", because a page authored after the move has no old URL to have
# been redirected from. The first post published after the move
# (moving-consciously-in-brazilian-zouk, 2026-08-01) hit exactly that and turned
# main red; no post between the 2026-07-25 capture and that date had exercised it.
#
# The fix is NOT to add a line to retired_urls.txt. That file documents itself as
# a capture of the tree immediately BEFORE the move, so a URL that never existed
# cannot honestly go in it, and doing so once means doing it for every future
# post until the file means nothing.
#
# This file is the acknowledgement list instead. A live /blogs/ URL passes AC 5.2
# if it is either the image of a retired URL or named here. Anything in neither
# still fails loudly, so the staleness check keeps its teeth: an accidental new
# page, a slug typo, or a stale baseline all still turn the test red.
#
# Entries are also checked in reverse: a URL listed here that the sitemap does
# NOT serve fails the test, so this file cannot rot into a pile of dead lines.
#
# Add the post's live URL here when you publish a new page under /blogs/.
# Blank lines and #-comments are ignored.

/blogs/moving-consciously-in-brazilian-zouk/
/blogs/brazilian-zouk-basic-timing-who-steps-first/
/blogs/are-you-really-dancing-or-just-moving/
/blogs/what-is-professionalism/
/blogs/why-major-cities-struggle-to-grow-brazilian-zouk/
